celery and redis are unpinned, and firebase-admin is only bounded below (>=6), while jinja2 is pinned 3.1.4.
SMTP timeout must be between 2s and 20s, because the relay may take 1.5s to greet and the Celery soft limit is 30s; the 300ms platform default would be too short.
The queue is in the shared replicated Redis, so backup null is acceptable.
Runs 3 Celery worker instances across 2 zones, owned by Team Growth, with empty overrides.
A live card-processor API key is hardcoded in plain text in the repo instead of being supplied via a ${NAME} environment placeholder.
Processor calls use a 4000ms timeout with 2 retries, i.e. 3 attempts.
Outbound calls go to https://api.cardprocessor.example/v2 with merchant ID HB-221-NL.
Dependencies are pinned: stripe-like sdk v1.14.2, zap v1.27.0, yaml.v3 v3.0.1, on go 1.23.
Config supports ${NAME} environment expansion, but the API key does not use it.
Needs at least 20/s per caller, and the empty overrides inherit http.default_rate_limit of none, so it is not throttled.
Idempotency keys are in shared Redis with AOF and the ledger in shared Postgres, snapshotted by the platform DBA team.
Runs 3 instances across 2 zones, owned by Team Money.
The image uses node:22-slim and runs npm install without a lockfile, so builds are not reproducible.
express is 'latest', decimal.js is '*', and demand-model-client is ^2.0.0, all floating, while only pino is pinned exactly.
The demand-model timeout must be at most 300ms because bookings-api waits only 400ms.
Overrides are empty, so it inherits the 300ms platform http.default_timeout, which sits exactly at the 300ms maximum with no margin.
Runs 2 instances across 2 zones, stateless, owned by Team Rentals.
The demand-model call over plain http uses PLATFORM_HTTP_TIMEOUT as its timeout, and on error falls back to a multiplier of 1.
parseDuration crashes if PLATFORM_HTTP_TIMEOUT is unset and treats any non-ms value as seconds.
